findings.title: Wrapper v2 execute() reads nonexistent release field runtime_identity; every future gated execution deterministically burns the single-use attempt into an unterminalized partial root
findings.evidence: scripts/research/f017_apple_serial_f32_capture_wrapper_v2.py line 273 builds attempt-start with release["runtime_identity"], but the bound release v2 (sha256 8896ccde...) has no such key (it has runtime_binding). Empirically reproduced with a synthetic temp-path release copy and synthetic authorization: KeyError('runtime_identity') is raised after exclusive mkdir of the attempt root and durable owner.json creation, before attempt-start.json and before the terminalizing try-block, so no terminal.json is written; a retry fails ATTEMPT_ALREADY_EXISTS_NO_RETRY. The resulting owner-present/start-absent state is exactly what the terminalizer rejects as DURABLE_START_INCOMPLETE_OPERATOR_ADJUDICATION_REQUIRED and what RN3 rule 5 forbids clearing, forcing operator adjudication and a replacement release identity. No committed test exercises execute() end-to-end (RN1 tests cover mkdir exclusivity and terminalizer functions only), and the banked validation ran --preflight-only, so the defect is invisible to the entire committed validation surface.
findings.required_action: Correct the field reference (bind attempt-start environment_identity to the release runtime_binding, or add a runtime_identity field to the release schema), regenerate the code manifest and release per the material-code-change rule, re-run validation, and add a synthetic end-to-end wrapper execute() test with a stubbed runner that would have caught this before any real approval or token can be considered.

findings.title: rope_base is the only load-bearing numeric constant of the S0-to-S2 graph left unpinned by every committed gate
findings.evidence: validate_package in f017-apple-serial-f32-capture.rs bit-pins position (0), attention_scale (0.0625), expert_weight_scale (2.5), heads/qk_nope/qk_rope/kv_lora/value_dim, and routed_expert_ids, but never checks rope_base; the package-schema contract fixed_graph likewise omits rope_base; the stage manifest pins RoPE order/rounding but no base value; the graph only requires rope_base > 0; no committed validator, prior boundary contract, or equivalence specification pins the numeric value (the synthetic test uses 1000000.0 but is not an authority). An operator-supplied package with any positive rope_base passes the binary preflight, wrapper, and all committed validators, and would produce wrong query_heads/key-rope bytes in the single no-retry attempt. This contradicts the architecture claim unresolved_load_bearing_semantics=[] and the executable-numeric-constants hardening standard applied to every peer constant.
findings.required_action: Pin the exact binary32 production rope_base in the package-schema fixed_graph, in validate_package (to_bits equality like attention_scale), and in the stage manifest RoPE row; revalidate. This must land with the F1 regeneration and before the approval/readiness phase.

findings.title: Spec text claims seven bound decoders including Q4_K; decoder-bindings contract binds six; the binary carries a Q4_K decode arm unreachable under package policy
findings.evidence: apple-production-serial-f32-capture-v1.md states decoders are bound for F32_LE, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0, IQ2_XXS, IQ3_XXS; the decoder-bindings contract and validator enforce exactly six formats without Q4_K; decode() in the capture binary implements Q4_K (144-byte blocks) but validate_package pins every one of the 40 tensor roles to a non-Q4_K encoding and rejects any extra or missing tensor, so the arm cannot execute in a valid run.
findings.required_action: At the next release generation, align the spec text to the six-format contract or remove the dead Q4_K arm from the binary so bytes, contract, and narrative agree.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: numerical authority and capture observability are governed by the per-role encoding/shape pins and the six hash-bound reachable decoders (dequant_q4_k additionally lives in cpu_dot.rs whose bytes are already hash-bound via the Q5_K binding); the discrepancy is documentation drift plus dead code, not a reachable alternate decode path, and the future execution gate is unaffected.

findings.title: Execution-time verification census gaps: no dylib read-back at --execute, and wrapper validate_release does not re-verify runtime_binding or bound_contracts hashes
findings.evidence: At execution time the binary string-compares package-claimed MLX identities against hardcoded constants but never hashes the actual dylibs it will load; the wrapper hashes code-manifest artifacts, authorization schema, and the executor, but not release.runtime_binding or the eight bound_contracts entries. A post-approval Homebrew upgrade would go undetected by the execution path itself.
findings.required_action: In the F1 regeneration, have the wrapper (or binary) hash /opt/homebrew libmlx/libmlxc against the runtime-binding constants immediately before spawn, and extend validate_release to cover runtime_binding and bound_contracts.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: the release chain explicitly assigns exact dylib/header read-back to the pre-approval readiness gate; the committed capture validator performs the machine read-back today (recomputed by this review: all five hashes match the pinned Homebrew installs); contracts are documentation whose drift cannot alter hash-bound executable bytes; and any post-approval library drift would surface in the ten-run determinism qualification and the frozen-tolerance comparison rather than producing a silent false PASS. Numerical authority, capture observability, accounting, and gate ordering remain intact; the recommendation removes an operator-procedure window, not an open bypass.

findings.title: Wrapper validate_capture checks count/uniqueness/ordinals but not the canonical stage-ID set, and does not sweep the capture root for unmanifested files
findings.evidence: validate_capture accepts any 34 unique stage_ids with correct ordinals, hashes, 0400 mode, nlink 1, and sizes; it does not compare the set against the canonical STAGE_IDS census and does not fail on extra files present in the capture root but absent from the manifest.
findings.required_action: At the next generation, pin the exact ordered canonical stage-ID list in validate_capture and reject unmanifested files in the capture root.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: the capture manifest is produced solely by the hash-bound executor whose in-graph census enforces the exact canonical 34 IDs exactly once (BTreeSet insert + STAGE_IDS membership + terminal seen-count check, verified in source and by synthetic test), files are created no-replace mode 0400 with post-write read-back by the same process, and the capture root must not pre-exist; wrapper-side set pinning would only defend against a compromised executor, which the executor hash gate already excludes.

findings.title: Expert gate/up/down matrices bypass DenseMatrix::validate at graph library level
findings.evidence: run_apple_serial_f32 calls validate() on the seven attention/router matrices only; routed and shared expert matrices rely on shape checks inside expert() and matvec, not on the values.len == rows*cols and finiteness validation.
findings.required_action: Add validate() over routed and shared expert matrices in the next code generation for library-level parity.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: in the bound production binary every expert tensor reaches the graph only through decode(), which enforces exact byte-length/shape-product geometry per pinned encoding and rejects any non-finite value, and every downstream stage output is finiteness-checked again at capture; the unvalidated path is reachable only by out-of-scope library callers such as tests, so numerical authority and capture observability of the frozen executor are unaffected.

findings.title: Code manifest omits some executable-contributing sources (e.g. crates/f017-runner/src/json.rs duplicate-key parser)
findings.evidence: The two-stage code manifest binds fifteen artifacts but not json.rs, whose parse_json_no_duplicates is load-bearing for package parsing in the executor; stream bridge and quant decoder sources are bound in the architecture and decoder contracts respectively but also absent from the code manifest.
findings.required_action: Enumerate json.rs (and other executable-reachable first-party sources) in the code manifest at the next generation.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: the binding chain is closed at two independent levels the manifest does not carry alone - the release pins execution_code_head (whole-commit source identity) and executor_sha256 (whole-binary identity, verified by the wrapper before spawn and recomputed by this review), so any drift in an unlisted source changes the executable hash and fails EXECUTOR_SHA; duplicate-key rejection semantics were additionally verified by direct source audit.

findings.title: Adjudication of compiler/Metal underspecification and backend-defined MLX matvec semantics
findings.evidence: MLX matvec reduction/contraction order and Rust f32 libm transcendental bytes (powf/sin/cos/exp/sqrt) are implementation-defined. The surface resolves them by declared exact-implementation authority: pinned dylib and header hashes (recomputed, matching), pinned macOS/Xcode/clang/rustc/metal identities in the runtime binding, inline(never) single-rounding scalar helpers that preclude FMA fusion across stage boundaries, serial left folds, thread limits pinned to 1, and an unexecuted ten-run byte-identity determinism qualification plus frozen numerical tolerances as future empirical gates. Portability across versions, devices, or compilers is explicitly not claimed.
findings.required_action: None beyond executing the already-frozen determinism qualification before any equivalence claim; residual Metal scheduling nondeterminism, if any, will fail that gate rather than pass silently.
findings.disposition: DOES_NOT_WEAKEN: the underspecification is openly declared, bounded to the pinned environment, and backstopped by byte-identity and tolerance gates that fail closed; the sole load-bearing constant found outside this declared resolution is rope_base, tracked separately as F2.

statement: APPLE PRODUCTION SERIAL-F32 CAPTURE SURFACE REJECTED FOR RELEASE-2: all 41 hash bindings, the 34-stage S0-to-S2 call graph, the 40-tensor census, the six reachable decoder bindings, retained-input open-once policy, RN1 ownership, receipt-derived accounting, ledger 175, wrapper-v1 tombstone, acyclic authorization chain, and all zero execution counters verified with no premature comparison, approval, or GO token; however the frozen wrapper v2 deterministically fails with KeyError runtime_identity after durable owner creation on every future gated execution, permanently consuming the single-use attempt into an unterminalized partial root (F1, BLOCKING, empirically confirmed), and the production rope_base numeric constant is unpinned by every committed gate (F2, NON_BLOCKING_REQUIRED); a corrected wrapper, pinned rope_base, regenerated code manifest and release, and a new validation and review cycle are required before any approval or readiness phase may proceed.
